limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.
rank over n=3 decks; no significance claim

judgment.argument: Convention first: this judgment is a weighted component, and 50 is the line where the measured components already say it. The measured components cannot see play: two games are logged where five are needed, nobody has surveyed a game for feel, and no Forge run describes the current list. The v1.1.0 cards are still arriving, so nothing has been played on it. That leaves the engine and the stacks. The thesis is coherent: bodies make the mana, cheap spells aimed at Zada turn each body into a card, and one payoff turn cashes the board in. Several stacks pass their checker with every card on the current list, and they cover the engine's own steps: the storm turn that Empty the Warrens ends, Fists of Flame as the lethal, and Witch's Mark copies at Zada. That is more than a thesis; the lines work as written. The Haze of Rage loop is off this list and I do not count it. Against that, kill_by_turn_8 reads 0.565, no stack proves an infinite, and no game has tested the list. Resilience is already the lowest component as capacity, so I do not deduct it again. A little above the line for the checked lines, no higher because nothing here has been played.
